sanskrit: vidma te śara pitaraṃ parjanyaṃ bhūriretasam | tenā te tanve śaṃ karaṃ pṛthivyāṃ te niṣecanaṃ bahiṣ ṭe astu bāl iti ||
english: We know your father, O arrow — Parjanya, rich in seed. By him I make wholeness for your body; may your discharge flow upon the earth; let what is bāl go outside.
By Indra, by Varuṇa, by Candra, and by Sūrya as well [is this healing accomplished].

sanskrit: yad āntreṣu gavīnyor yad vastāv adhi saṃsrutam | (…) ||
english: Whatever has collected in the intestines, in the two flanks, whatever has gathered in the bladder — [may it flow out] (remainder lost).

sanskrit: pra te bhinadmi mehanaṃ vartraṃ veśantyā iva | tenā te tanve śaṃ karaṃ pṛthivyāṃ te niṣecanaṃ bahiṣ ṭe astu bāl iti ||
english: I burst open your urinary passage, the obstruction, as [one opens] a channel. By that I make wholeness for your body; may your discharge flow upon the earth; let what is bāl go outside.

sanskrit: yatheṣukā parāpatad avasṛṣṭādhi dhanvanaḥ | evā te mūtraṃ mucyatāṃ bahir bāl iti sarvakam ||
english: As an arrow flies away, released from the bow, so may your urine be released — outward, all of it, bāl.

sanskrit: vaṣaṭ te pūṣann asyai suvṛktim aryamā hotā kṛṇotu vedhāḥ | sisratāṃ nāry utapradātā vi parvāṇi jihatāṃ sūtavā u ||
english: Vaṣaṭ! O Pūṣan, may Aryamā — the skilled hotṛ, the Disposer — fashion a fine recitation for her. May the birth-giver flow forth; may the joints open wide for her giving birth.

sanskrit: catasro diśaḥ pradiśaś catasro bhūmyā uta | devā garbhaṃ sam airayan te vy ūrṇuvantu sūtave ||
english: The four directions and four quarter-directions, and those of the earth as well — the gods have brought the embryo together; may those very ones open it wide for her to give birth.

sanskrit: suṣṭā vy ūrṇotu vi yoniṃ hāpayāmasi | śrathayā sūṣaṇe tvam ava tvaṃ viṣkale sṛja ||
english: May she who is prepared open wide; we loosen the womb. Relax [it], O Sūṣaṇa; and you, O Viṣkala, let [the child] go free.

sanskrit: neva snāvasu parvasu na keśeṣu nakheṣu ca | avaitu pṛśni śevalaṃ śune jarāyv attave ||
english: Not in the sinews, not in the joints, not in the hair, not in the nails — may the variegated membrane fall away, for a dog to devour the afterbirth.

sanskrit: neva māṃse na pīvasi neva kasmiṃś canāyatam | ava jarāyu padyatām ||
english: Not in the flesh, not in the fat, not clinging to anything whatsoever — may the afterbirth fall down.

sanskrit: ye triṣaptāḥ pariyanti viśvā rūpāṇi bibhrataḥ | vācaspatir balā teṣāṃ tanvam adya dadhātu me ||
english: Those three-times-seven who go about bearing all forms — may Vācaspati place their strengths into my body today.

sanskrit: upa na ehi vācaspate devena manasā saha | asoṣpate ni ramaya mayy eva tanvaṃ mama ||
english: Come near to us, O Vācaspati, together with the divine mind. O lord of the breath-utterance, make it rest within me; within me alone — my body.

sanskrit: ihaivābhi vi tanu- -ubhe ārtnī iva jyayā | vācaspatir ni yacchatu mayy eva tanvaṃ mama ||
english: Stretch forth here in both directions, as two bow-tips by the bowstring. May Vācaspati hold [them] fast within me; within me alone — my body.

sanskrit: upahūto vācaspatir upahūto 'haṃ vacaspatyuḥ | saṃ śrutena rādhiṣīya mā śrutena vi rādhiṣi ||
english: Vācaspati is invoked; I, the devotee of Vācaspati, am invoked. May I succeed together with my renown; may I not fail through my renown.
